qualitative.source: claude-code subagent (viewed all 4 contact sheets + profile + transcript)
qualitative.summary: A 31-minute 'pov' diary of a working trip through Australia (hinterland, Melbourne, Sydney). A ~25 s teaser with a song (forest walk, a yellow 'MELBOURNE' card, cooking) leads into a four-minute garden sit-down with a notebook, where he reviews his year and plans. The middle is talk-heavy home and apartment footage (night desk monologues lit by screens and lamps, low-angle laptop talks) broken by 'FLIGHT DAY' and '9AM' cards. The set piece is a Melbourne fan meetup announced by an Instagram story. It ends with a walking-then-standing monologue in a Sydney car park, ending 'thank you for watching'.
qualitative.hook_analysis: Music teaser rather than a spoken claim: forest walk (0:00), a rounded-frame street shot with bold yellow 'MELBOURNE' (0:10) and kitchen prep (0:20) under captioned song lyrics; speech begins ~0:03 under the music and the premise ('currently down in Australia') arrives by ~0:30. The hook is the place card and the personality, not jeopardy.
qualitative.narrative_arc: Chronological: hinterland reflection on the year (0:30-4:18) -> friends at a brick loft (5:08-6:07) -> notebook 'golden rule' (6:17) -> plan to fly to Melbourne (7:46) -> night work talks (8:36-12:54) -> FLIGHT DAY (13:04) -> apartment desk talk on business systems (14:13-17:41) -> story announcing a meetup (17:51) -> street meetup and group photo (18:11-23:29) -> 9AM rental car (25:08-26:07) -> Sydney walk and car-park monologue on a 'North star' (26:37-30:45).
qualitative.camera_and_composition: Locked-off wide-angle medium on a low stool in a garden (0:30-4:18); ultra-wide upward selfies with ceiling lights (4:28-4:48, 14:03); close desk framing with screen reflection in glasses (9:55-12:54); low-angle laptop-cam framing against bright windows (14:13-17:41); eye-level handheld two-shots at the meetup (18:11-23:39). Rounded-corner inserts at 0:10, 13:24, 19:21, 25:57. Exact cuts/moves not observable at storyboard resolution.
qualitative.color_and_grade: Warm, natural greens by day; nights are dark amber with practical lamps (27% low-key frames). Street scenes in Melbourne are bright, punchy daylight. Modest contrast, warm bias (warmth 0.087).
qualitative.sound_and_music: Densest talk of the set: ~98% speech coverage at ~176 wpm. Music is a bed under the teaser (song lyrics captioned) and a short speech-free passage around 26:05-26:18. Captions occasionally carry speaker handles ('@brunocasanovas', '@matthardybrown').
what_to_borrow: 10-20 s teaser with a bold yellow place card before the talk
Day/time cards ('FLIGHT DAY', '9AM') as chapter markers
Name the people on screen in caption form with their handle
Use the fan meetup as the film's social set piece, set up earlier by a story screenshot
End with a standing to-camera wrap in a neutral location
what_to_avoid_copying: Four-minute static garden sit-down at the top - for travel films cover it with b-roll
Long night monologues lit by a laptop screen (9:55-12:54)
Calls to action (email list) inside the story

qualitative.source: claude-code subagent (viewed all 5 contact sheets + profile + transcript)
qualitative.summary: A 34-minute 'pov' diary of a working holiday in Bali/Lombok with business partners and friends. It opens on a ~30 s music-led lead-in (snorkelling, a dark villa, a sunset silhouette) whose shots recur near the end, then settles into captioned conversation in a co-working space. The body alternates business talk (a new venture reveal, a standing revenue/'building in public' update in front of a hillside window, a team video call) with leisure: boat trips, gym, villa inspections, tennis, cliff-jumping. Yellow condensed time cards ('3PM', 'NEXT MORNING') mark days, and burned-in captions run throughout. It closes on a boat in a straw hat with a toast and 'see you in the next one'.
qualitative.hook_analysis: Short visual lead-in rather than a spoken claim: 0:00-0:30 shows snorkel gear on a boat, a silhouetted villa interior and a sunset silhouette, under a song (captions transcribe 'Fly Me to the Moon' lyrics). Several images (snorkel 0:10 ~ 31:04, sunset silhouette 0:30 ~ 27:26) reappear later, so it works as a teaser of the payoff. Speech arrives at ~0:04 but the first chapter is conversational, so the hook is mood plus title premise, not a stated stake.
qualitative.narrative_arc: Chronological multi-day diary with chapters: intro chat -> venture reveal (2:09) -> Lombok boat day -> standing business update (7:56-10:35) -> gym -> villa/property inspection (12:34-17:41) -> team call (18:21-21:49) -> leisure/tennis -> 'NEXT MORNING' travel day with flight, forest swim -> sunset reflection on starting a business (27:16-28:46) -> boat/snorkel finale and toast. Business beats and fun beats alternate every few minutes; the resolution is a spoken reflection on work-life balance.
qualitative.camera_and_composition: Mostly handheld wide-angle: low-angle selfies under a boat canopy (4:28-6:47), over-the-shoulder group shots, a locked-off medium of the creator standing against a bright window with hills (7:56-10:35) that leaves the face partly silhouetted. Laptop screens of a video call shot straight-on (18:21-20:50). Occasional rounded-corner 'film frame' inserts (0:10, 14:43, 16:12). Exact camera moves and cuts are not observable at storyboard resolution; motion-blurred frames at 14:53 and 17:51 suggest whip moves between scenes.
qualitative.color_and_grade: Warm, slightly muted naturalistic grade (profile warmth 0.064, saturation 0.34); overcast Lombok greens and creams, warm wood interiors, deep orange sunset silhouettes (27:16-28:46). Window shots are allowed to blow out rather than be relit.
qualitative.sound_and_music: Speech covers ~88% of runtime at ~131 wpm. Music is a bed under the opening (song lyrics captioned) and short speech-free passages (0:40-1:27 per profile, 14:47-15:01, 17:41-17:55, 23:21-23:35). Caption markers include applause and laughter. Audio itself not available.
what_to_borrow: Open on 20-30 s of music and strong images pulled from later in the film, then drop into casual talk
Bold yellow condensed time/day cards ('3PM', 'NEXT MORNING') to orient a multi-day edit
Alternate a work beat with a leisure beat every few minutes so talk-heavy sections breathe
Burned-in captions for overlapping group chatter
Bookend with matching imagery (sunset, snorkel) so the ending feels like a payoff of the opening
what_to_avoid_copying: Three-minute standing talking head against a blown-out window (7:56-10:35) - expose for the face or cover with b-roll
Revenue and business-performance monologues that only make sense for an entrepreneur audience
Screen-recorded video calls as long scenes - visually static

qualitative.source: claude-code subagent (viewed all 4 contact sheets + profile + transcript)
qualitative.summary: A 27:45 'business trip' diary across Berlin, a grandmother's home in Poland, and Barcelona. A music-led montage (apartment, guest, gym) gives way to gym banter and a sit-down interview with a founder friend. Yellow cards ('10:30AM', 'NEXT DAY', 'BABCIU', 'BERLIN AIRPORT') segment the days. The emotional centre is a frank four-minute couch monologue about working 16-hour days, followed by a road trip to a friend's grandma. Barcelona brings metro, beach and lunch, and the film ends in a car promising the next episode.
qualitative.hook_analysis: Visual lead-in with music (0:00-0:14: rounded-frame apartment, hallway, guest greeting), then a light spoken setup ('in Berlin with...') and gym banter. Most-replayed segment is the first ~17 s, so the montage itself is the hook; there is no stated stake.
qualitative.narrative_arc: Berlin morning and gym (0:00-1:39) -> friend interview (1:49-4:08) -> 10:30AM retail store (4:18-4:28) -> evening car (4:38-5:07) -> NEXT DAY run (5:17-6:17) -> couch confession on pressure (6:46-10:44) -> drive to Poland (10:54-12:43) -> BABCIU dinner (12:53-14:12) -> hometown drive (14:22-16:41) -> packing and farewell (16:51-18:00) -> BERLIN AIRPORT (18:10) -> Barcelona plan, metro, beach, lunch (18:30-26:46) -> car ending as a cliff-hanger (27:05-27:35).
qualitative.camera_and_composition: Two-shot interview framing in an industrial gym (1:49-4:08); locked-off medium on a couch (6:46-10:44); dashboard wide two-shots in cars (10:54-16:31); low wide selfies on the metro platform and beach (20:59-25:16). Rounded-corner inserts at 0:00, 1:39, 4:28, 12:53, 18:10. Cuts/moves not observable at storyboard resolution.
qualitative.color_and_grade: Warm beige/tan palette (palette #bea484), moderate saturation, almost no low-key footage (5%). Barcelona daylight is bright and blue-skied; Berlin interiors warm tungsten.
qualitative.sound_and_music: ~91% speech at ~157 wpm; music caption markers at the open and a ~14 s speech-free beat around 24:10-24:24. Captions include censored expletives.
what_to_borrow: Yellow day/time/place cards including personal names ('BABCIU') as chapter headings
A seated friend interview to add a second voice
Car dashboard two-shots for relaxed conversation during transit
End by setting up the next video
what_to_avoid_copying: Shirtless selfie coverage as the dominant Barcelona imagery
Ending on 'start a new video from here' without resolution if the film must stand alone

qualitative.source: claude-code subagent (viewed all 2 contact sheets + profile + transcript)
qualitative.summary: A 15:45 reflective piece in three movements: a Himalayan trek, a fan meetup in Kathmandu, and a late-night sit-down in Hong Kong. It opens on wide mountain landscapes with the creator in awe, then a philosophical voiceover (a quote about thinking versus listening) runs over monastery and village b-roll. The middle is a long ultra-wide low-angle selfie monologue against blue sky, an Instagram-story announcement and a warm, crowded night meetup. The final five minutes are a locked-off talk at a red booth with his sign-off giving name, date and city.
qualitative.hook_analysis: Spoken cold open over spectacle: wide Himalayan valley shots (0:00-0:10) with a gasped 'most beautiful thing' line, then straight into a borrowed philosophical voiceover across monastery, monks playing football, a waterfall shower and a couple portrait (0:20-1:29). The hook is awe plus an idea, not a plan; it is the most cinematic opening of the six.
qualitative.narrative_arc: Retreat -> reflection -> community -> solitude. Trek montage (0:00-1:29) -> selfie reflection on connection (1:38-4:55) -> story announcement of a meetup (5:05) -> Kathmandu errands and meetup (5:15-10:30) -> night garden music beat (10:40-10:50) -> Hong Kong skyline transition (11:00-11:09) -> red-booth sit-down with plans (coffee-table book, events) and the sign-off.
qualitative.camera_and_composition: Wide static landscapes with a figure from behind; ultra-wide low-angle selfie with sky filling the top of frame (1:38-4:55); handheld crowd coverage in tungsten interiors (7:52-10:30); window silhouette over the Hong Kong skyline (11:00); a locked-off medium at table height in a red booth (11:19-15:35). Cuts and moves are not observable at storyboard resolution.
qualitative.color_and_grade: Two worlds: daylight Himalayan earth tones with blue sky, then low-key warm/red nights (profile: 48% low-key frames, high saturation 0.50, flat contrast, red-heavy palette). The booth section is deep red with practical light; a red light spills on his face at 13:17-13:27.
qualitative.sound_and_music: Opening uses a voiceover quote rather than his own talk; music caption markers around the night montage (~9:05-11:00, song lyric captions). Overall speech coverage ~88% at ~134 wpm; longest non-speech gap ~26 s.
what_to_borrow: Lead with your single most spectacular landscape and an unscripted reaction
Lay a reflective voiceover over b-roll of local life to set a theme
Hard contrast between a daylight journey and a low-key night reflection for the ending
Sign off with name, date and city as a diary signature
what_to_avoid_copying: Borrowed voiceover of someone else's speech - rights and authenticity issues; write your own
Three-plus minutes of a single selfie angle (1:38-4:55) without cutaways
Mood-heavy red low-key grade where faces get muddy at small sizes

qualitative.source: claude-code subagent (viewed all 5 contact sheets + profile + transcript)
qualitative.summary: A 35:40 trip film built around one warm human scene: visiting a Chinese 'auntie' near a highway toll gate, conducted in Chinese with translated subtitles. It opens with a short music lead-in, then long in-car talk about China's market, then ~10 minutes of the auntie visit (fruit, laughter, farewells). After a warehouse visit and an airport sit-down, red '香港'/'HONG KONG' cards move the story to Hong Kong for a roadside brand update. The last ten minutes are a single call-booth monologue on entrepreneurship ending 'another week showing up'.
qualitative.hook_analysis: Short visual lead-in (apartment wide, pillarboxed street shot 0:00-0:10) under music, then a casual 'good morning' and the plan to stop and see auntie by 0:20. The title carries the hook (grandma + speaking Chinese); the video withholds that scene until ~5:30.
qualitative.narrative_arc: Road trip (0:20-4:59) -> arrival and phone call to auntie (5:09-6:48) -> auntie visit and farewell (6:58-16:25) -> facility/warehouse (16:35-18:15) -> airport talk and chat with a stranger (18:25-21:24) -> HONG KONG cards (21:44, 22:04) -> roadside brand update (22:14-24:33) -> office BTS (24:43-25:13) -> call-booth reflection to the end (25:23-35:30).
qualitative.camera_and_composition: Mixed aspect ratios: many pillarboxed frames (1:10-2:39, 16:45-18:15, 21:54-22:04, 24:43-24:53) suggest vertical/phone or different-camera footage placed in 16:9. In-car side angle from the back seat; observational wide handheld at the gate; a radial/zoom-blurred frame at 8:18 hints at a stylised transition; static medium in the booth. Exact cuts not observable at storyboard resolution.
qualitative.color_and_grade: The warmest and most colourful of the set (warmth 0.143, colourfulness 48): golden low winter sun at the gate, saturated yellow shop wall (5:28-6:28), a cool grey airport, and an amber booth with tungsten light.
qualitative.sound_and_music: Lowest speech coverage (74%), many laughter (31) and music/singing markers; several 13-35 s speech-free passages during the auntie scenes (profile 5:55-16:35) let ambience and music carry the moment. Chinese dialogue is translated in captions prefixed 'Chinese:'.
what_to_borrow: Let a warm human encounter play long with few cuts and translated subtitles
Drop narration and let music and laughter carry emotional scenes
Bold red bilingual city cards to mark a border crossing
A stranger conversation in a waiting area as a light interlude
what_to_avoid_copying: Ten-minute single-angle booth monologue as the ending
Unplanned mix of pillarboxed and full-frame footage
Withholding the title's promise for five minutes of car talk

qualitative.source: claude-code subagent (viewed all 4 contact sheets + profile + transcript)
qualitative.summary: A 26:12 'pov' episode: a day trip from Hong Kong into Shenzhen for a tech conference, then a fan run in Bali/Indonesia, and a sober closing reflection. It opens with a palm-payment moment at a convenience store (repeated later in context) after a brief office lead-in. The middle crosses the border, rides in a chauffeured car with translated Chinese dialogue, shows him on a conference stage screen, and announces a 6 a.m. meetup run via an Instagram story. A desk explainer with a screen recording leads to the dawn run with a crowd. The final four minutes are a bookshelf sit-down admitting low energy and struggles.
qualitative.hook_analysis: Lead-in then a novelty: office wides (0:00-0:10) then paying by palm at a 7-Eleven (0:20-0:49) with surprised reactions and 'Chinese:' subtitles; the same scene is replayed in place at 11:02-11:22, so the opening is a flash-forward teaser of a curious moment. Most-replayed segment is the first ~16 s.
qualitative.narrative_arc: Office/new CFO (0:59-1:09) -> drive and border crossing (1:19-5:06) -> back-seat ride with a driver (5:26-7:45) -> passport insert (8:14-8:34) -> SHENZHEN card (8:54) -> conference (9:04-10:53) -> palm pay in context (11:02) -> night hotel/car (11:42-12:51) -> story announcing run (13:11) -> desk explainer with screen recording (13:41-18:08) -> '29TH OF JULY' dawn run (18:17-21:15) -> plane/contract inserts (21:25-21:55) -> bookshelf reflection and sign-off (22:05-26:02).
qualitative.camera_and_composition: Driver-side profile shots in a car (1:19-3:28); rear-seat wide with sunroof (5:26-7:45); hand inserts of passport stamps; stage shot with his name on screen (10:03-10:23); static desk medium with picture-in-picture screen recording (16:19-17:18); wide locked-off street shot of the crowd at dawn (18:27-20:06); final static medium ending with him reaching to the camera (26:02). Rounded-corner inserts at 0:00, 21:25, 21:45. Cut detail not observable at storyboard resolution.
qualitative.color_and_grade: Mostly neutral to cool and darker (brightness 0.29, 21% low-key) - car interiors, conference halls, night hotels - with a sodium-orange dawn street at the meetup and a pink-lit bookshelf at the end.
qualitative.sound_and_music: ~82% speech at ~128 wpm; speech-free music passages at the open (0:08-0:34), entering the conference (8:59-9:52) and at the run (~21:30). Translated 'Chinese:' captions for dialogue.
what_to_borrow: Open on a novel local moment and replay it in context later
Passport/border inserts to mark a crossing
Bold yellow date card ('29TH OF JULY') over a dark establishing shot
Wide locked-off shot of a gathered crowd while you speak to them
End on an honest low-energy reflection rather than a hype outro
what_to_avoid_copying: Screen-recording explainers inside a travel story
Long talk from the back seat of a car (2+ min) with one angle
Pivoting countries mid-film without a clear bridge
